title: Symphony of colors in the Tarantula
caption: The Tarantula Nebula, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope and ESO's New Technology Telescope
celestial: Hodge 301, R136, Tarantula Nebula · constellation Dorado · about 170000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Just above the center of this mosaic sits R136, a huge cluster of very hot stars, while near the lower edge lies an older cluster, Hodge 301, wrapped in filaments and sheets of gas. This is the Tarantula Nebula in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a smallish irregular galaxy 170,000 light-years away. Even without a telescope, the nebula shows up as a big, milky smudge.

The stars in R136 are among the most massive known, and the cluster is young. Its oldest stars are only about 5 million years old, and its smallest are still forming. Hodge 301 is almost 10 times older. Some of its stars have already exploded as supernovae, and the shockwave compressed nearby gas into the filaments seen around it.

Astronomers believe the Large Magellanic Cloud is in a violent phase. Close encounters with the Milky Way, which it orbits, are thought to have triggered a burst of star formation, part of which is visible in the Tarantula.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (5.32 x 4.32 arcminutes) and distance (170000 light years), the frame spans roughly 263 × 214 light-years. Its light set out about 170,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light mosaic uses three narrow-band filters from Hubble's WFPC2, with ionized oxygen shown as blue, hydrogen-alpha as green and ionized sulfur as red.
understand.eye: An eye would see hydrogen's glow as red, not green, and the narrow filters separate individual elements in a way the eye cannot.

behind.people: See full credit: ESA/NASA, ESO and Danny LaCrue
behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The mosaic was created by 23-year-old amateur astronomer Danny LaCrue from 15 exposures by Hubble's Wide Field and Planetary Camera 2, laid over matching images from ESO's New Technology Telescope at La Silla. Each Hubble exposure lasted between 800 and 2800 seconds per filter.
alt: A colorful nebula with a dense cluster of bright stars just above center and an older star cluster near the lower edge surrounded by filaments of gas.
